sanskrit: tataḥ sukhāsīnam ṛṣiṃ vāgyatau saṃvavāhatuḥ na ca paryāptam ity āha bhārgavaḥ sumahātapāḥ
english: Then, holding their speech in check, the two attended upon the sage as he sat at his ease; yet Bhārgava, of mighty austerities, said it was not enough.

sanskrit: yadā tau nirvikārau tu lakṣayām āsa bhārgavaḥ tata utthāya sahasā snānaśālāṃ viveśa ha kḷptam eva tu tatrāsīt snānīyaṃ pārthivocitam
english: When Bhārgava observed that the two remained unmoved, he rose all at once and entered the bathing-chamber; there the bathing appointments, befitting a king, stood already made ready.

sanskrit: asatkṛtya tu tat sarvaṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata sa muniḥ punar evātha nṛpateḥ paśyatas tadā nāsūyāṃ cakratus tau ca daṃpatī bharatarṣabha
english: But the sage, scorning all that, vanished from the very spot once more before the king's eyes; and the royal couple, O bull of the Bharatas, harbored no resentment.

sanskrit: atha snātaḥ sa bhagavān siṃhāsanagataḥ prabhuḥ darśayām āsa kuśikaṃ sabhāryaṃ bhṛgunandanaḥ
english: Then, having bathed, the venerable lord, the delight of the Bhṛgus, seated upon a lion-throne, showed himself to Kuśika and his wife.

sanskrit: saṃhṛṣṭavadano rājā sabhāryaḥ kuśiko munim siddham annam iti prahvo nirvikāro nyavedayat
english: With a glad countenance, King Kuśika, together with his wife, bowed low and unperturbed announced to the sage that the meal was prepared.

sanskrit: ānīyatām iti munis taṃ covāca narādhipam rājā ca samupājahre tadannaṃ saha bhāryayā
english: "Let it be brought," the sage said to that lord of men; and the king, together with his wife, fetched forth that food.

sanskrit: māṃsaprakārān vividhāñ śākāni vividhāni ca vesavāravikārāṃś ca pānakāni laghūni ca
english: Many kinds of meat dishes, and vegetables of many kinds, and preparations richly spiced, and light beverages,

sanskrit: rasālāpūpakāṃś citrān modakān atha ṣāḍavān rasān nānāprakārāṃś ca vanyaṃ ca munibhojanam
english: varied sweet cakes, and sweetmeats, and the six-flavored relishes, and juices of every sort, and the wild forest fare fit for a sage.

sanskrit: phalāni ca vicitrāṇi tathā bhojyāni bhūriśaḥ badareṅgudakāśmaryabhallātakavaṭāni ca
english: And fruits of many kinds, and other foods in abundance—jujubes, iṅgudas, kāśmarya berries, marking-nuts, and banyan figs—

sanskrit: gṛhasthānāṃ ca yad bhojyaṃ yac cāpi vanavāsinām sarvam āhārayām āsa rājā śāpabhayān muneḥ
english: whatever food belongs to householders and whatever belongs to forest-dwellers—the king had all of it brought, in dread of the sage's curse.

sanskrit: atha sarvam upanyastam agrataś cyavanasya tat tataḥ sarvaṃ samānīya tac ca śayyāsanaṃ muniḥ
english: Then all of it was set out before Cyavana; whereupon the sage gathered up the whole of it, along with the couch and the seat,

sanskrit: vastraiḥ śubhair avacchādya bhojanopaskaraiḥ saha sarvam ādīpayām āsa cyavano bhṛgunandanaḥ
english: and, having covered it over with fine garments together with the vessels of the meal, Cyavana, the delight of the Bhṛgus, set the whole of it ablaze.

sanskrit: na ca tau cakratuḥ kopaṃ daṃpatī sumahāvratau tayoḥ saṃprekṣator eva punar antarhito 'bhavat
english: Yet the couple, steadfast in their great vow, gave way to no anger; and even as the two looked on, he vanished once again.

sanskrit: tatraiva ca sa rājarṣis tasthau tāṃ rajanīṃ tadā sabhāryo vāgyataḥ śrīmān na ca taṃ kopa āviśat
english: And in that very place the royal sage stood through that night, with his wife, silent and glorious; nor did anger enter into him.

sanskrit: nityaṃ saṃskṛtam annaṃ tu vividhaṃ rājaveśmani śayanāni ca mukhyāni pariṣekāś ca puṣkalāḥ
english: Day after day the dressed food of many kinds, and the finest couches, and lavish baths were furnished in the royal dwelling,

sanskrit: vastraṃ ca vividhākāram abhavat samupārjitam na śaśāka tato draṣṭum antaraṃ cyavanas tadā
english: and garments of every fashion were procured; and Cyavana could find no flaw therein to seize upon.

sanskrit: punar eva ca viprarṣiḥ provāca kuśikaṃ nṛpam sabhāryo māṃ rathenāśu vaha yatra bravīmy aham
english: Then once more the brahman-sage said to King Kuśika: "With your wife, convey me swiftly by chariot to wherever I direct."

sanskrit: tatheti ca prāha nṛpo nirviśaṅkas tapodhanam krīḍāratho 'stu bhagavann uta sāṃgrāmiko rathaḥ
english: "So be it," said the king, without misgiving, to that ascetic rich in penance. "Shall it be a pleasure-chariot, O venerable one, or a war-chariot?"

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa munis tena rājñā hṛṣṭena tad vacaḥ cyavanaḥ pratyuvācedaṃ hṛṣṭaḥ parapuraṃjayam
english: Thus addressed by that gladdened king, the sage Cyavana, well pleased, made this reply to the conqueror of hostile cities:

sanskrit: sajjīkuru rathaṃ kṣipraṃ yas te sāṃgrāmiko mataḥ sāyudhaḥ sapatākaś ca saśaktiḥ kaṇayaṣṭimān
english: "Make ready at once the chariot that you reckon a war-chariot—furnished with weapons, with banners, with a lance, and with a barbed javelin,

sanskrit: kiṅkiṇīśatanirghoṣo yuktas tomarakalpanaiḥ gadākhaḍganibaddhaś ca parameṣuśatānvitaḥ
english: resounding with a hundred bells, fitted with arrays of pikes, bound about with mace and sword, and supplied with hundreds of choice arrows."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa taṃ tathety uktvā kalpayitvā mahāratham bhāryāṃ vāme dhuri tadā cātmānaṃ dakṣiṇe tathā
english: Then he, saying "So be it," made ready the great chariot, and set his wife at the left of the yoke and himself at the right,

sanskrit: tridaṃṣṭraṃ vajrasūcyagraṃ pratodaṃ tatra cādadhat sarvam etat tato dattvā nṛpo vākyam athābravīt
english: and took up there a goad three-pronged and sharp as an adamant needle at its point. Having given all this over, the king then spoke these words:

sanskrit: bhagavan kva ratho yātu bravītu bhṛgunandanaḥ yatra vakṣyasi viprarṣe tatra yāsyati te rathaḥ
english: "Venerable one, where shall the chariot go? Let the delight of the Bhṛgus declare it. Wherever you shall say, O brahman-sage, there shall your chariot go."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu bhagavān pratyuvācātha taṃ nṛpam itaḥprabhṛti yātavyaṃ padakaṃ padakaṃ śanaiḥ
english: Thus addressed, the venerable one replied to that king: "From here onward you must go step by step, slowly,

sanskrit: śramo mama yathā na syāt tathā me chandacāriṇau sukhaṃ caivāsmi voḍhavyo janaḥ sarvaś ca paśyatu
english: so that no fatigue may come to me. Move at my pleasure, you two; I am to be drawn in comfort, and let all the people look on."

sanskrit: notsāryaḥ pathikaḥ kaś cit tebhyo dāsyāmy ahaṃ vasu brāhmaṇebhyaś ca ye kāmān arthayiṣyanti māṃ pathi
english: "No traveler is to be thrust aside; to them I shall give wealth—to the brahmans too who shall beg of me their desires along the way.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ dāsyāmy aśeṣeṇa dhanaṃ ratnāni caiva hi kriyatāṃ nikhilenaitan mā vicāraya pārthiva
english: I shall give it all without remainder, the wealth and the jewels alike. Let this be done in full; do not deliberate, O king."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rājā bhṛtyān athābravīt yad yad brūyān munis tat tat sarvaṃ deyam aśaṅkitaiḥ
english: Hearing that word of his, the king then said to his servants: "Whatever the sage may ask, all of it is to be given without hesitation."

sanskrit: tato ratnāny anekāni striyo yugyam ajāvikam kṛtākṛtaṃ ca kanakaṃ gajendrāś cācalopamāḥ
english: Then jewels beyond number, women, draught-teams, goats and sheep, gold both wrought and unwrought, and lordly elephants like mountains,

sanskrit: anvagacchanta tam ṛṣiṃ rājāmātyāś ca sarvaśaḥ hāhābhūtaṃ ca tat sarvam āsīn nagaram ārtimat
english: and the king's ministers, all of them, followed after that sage; and the whole city became a tumult of grief, struck with anguish.

sanskrit: tau tīkṣṇāgreṇa sahasā pratodena pracoditau pṛṣṭhe viddhau kaṭe caiva nirvikārau tam ūhatuḥ
english: Goaded all at once by the sharp-pointed prod, pierced upon the back and on the hip, the two, unmoved, drew him along.

sanskrit: vepamānau virāhārau pañcāśad rātrakarśitau kathaṃ cid ūhatur vīrau daṃpatī taṃ rathottamam
english: Trembling, gone without food, wasted by fifty nights, the heroic couple drew that surpassing chariot with utmost difficulty.

sanskrit: bahuśo bhṛśaviddhau tau kṣaramāṇau kṣatodbhavam dadṛśāte mahārāja puṣpitāv iva kiṃśukau
english: Pierced again and again and grievously, oozing the blood sprung from their wounds, they appeared, O great king, like two kiṃśuka trees in flower.

sanskrit: tau dṛṣṭvā pauravargas tu bhṛśaṃ śokaparāyaṇaḥ abhiśāpabhayāt trasto na ca kiṃ cid uvāca ha
english: Beholding the two, the townsfolk were utterly given over to grief; yet, terrified by the dread of his curse, they said nothing at all.

sanskrit: dvandvaśaś cābruvan sarve paśyadhvaṃ tapaso balam kruddhā api muniśreṣṭhaṃ vīkṣituṃ naiva śaknumaḥ
english: And all of them said, two by two: "Behold the power of penance! Though wrathful, we cannot so much as look upon this best of sages."

sanskrit: aho bhagavato vīryaṃ maharṣer bhāvitātmanaḥ rājñaś cāpi sabhāryasya dhairyaṃ paśyata yādṛśam
english: "Ah, the might of the venerable great sage of perfected soul! And behold too what fortitude the king, with his wife, displays!"

sanskrit: śrāntāv api hi kṛcchreṇa ratham etaṃ samūhatuḥ na caitayor vikāraṃ vai dadarśa bhṛgunandanaḥ
english: For though spent, with great hardship they drew this chariot onward; yet the delight of the Bhṛgus saw in the two no change of heart.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tataḥ sa nirvikārau tau dṛṣṭvā bhṛgukulodvahaḥ vasu viśrāṇayām āsa yathā vaiśravaṇas tathā
english: Bhīṣma said: Then, seeing the two unmoved, the upholder of the Bhṛgu line dispensed wealth as Vaiśravaṇa himself might do.

sanskrit: tatrāpi rājā prītātmā yathājñaptam athākarot tato 'sya bhagavān prīto babhūva munisattamaḥ
english: In that too the king, glad of heart, did as he was bidden; whereupon the venerable one, that best of sages, grew pleased with him.

sanskrit: avatīrya rathaśreṣṭhād daṃpatī tau mumoca ha vimocya caitau vidhivat tato vākyam uvāca ha
english: Descending from that finest of chariots, he released the couple; and having freed them duly, he then spoke these words.

sanskrit: snigdhagambhīrayā vācā bhārgavaḥ suprasannayā dadāni vāṃ varaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ tad brūtām iti bhārata
english: In a voice tender, deep, and most serene, Bhārgava said: "Let me grant the two of you a choicest boon; name it," O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sukumārau ca tau vidvān karābhyāṃ munisattamaḥ pasparśāmṛtakalpābhyāṃ snehād bharatasattama
english: And that best of sages, the knowing one, touched the two tender ones with his hands, hands like ambrosia, out of affection, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: athābravīn nṛpo vākyaṃ śramo nāsty āvayor iha viśrāntau svaḥ prabhāvāt te dhyānenaiveti bhārgava
english: Then the king spoke: "There is no weariness in us two here; by your power, O Bhārgava, by your very meditation, we are wholly rested."

sanskrit: atha tau bhagavān prāha prahṛṣṭaś cyavanas tadā na vṛthā vyāhṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ yan mayā tad bhaviṣyati
english: Then the venerable Cyavana, greatly delighted, said to the two: "What I declared before was not spoken in vain; it shall come to pass.

sanskrit: ramaṇīyaḥ samuddeśo gaṅgātīram idaṃ śubham kaṃ cit kālaṃ vrataparo nivatsyāmīha pārthiva
english: Delightful is this spot, this fair bank of the Gaṅgā; for some time, intent upon my vow, I shall dwell here, O king.

sanskrit: gamyatāṃ svapuraṃ putra viśrāntaḥ punar eṣyasi ihasthaṃ māṃ sabhāryas tvaṃ draṣṭāsi śvo narādhipa
english: Go to your own city, my son; rested, you shall return. Tomorrow, with your wife, you shall behold me abiding here, O lord of men.

sanskrit: na ca manyus tvayā kāryaḥ śreyas te samupasthitam yat kāṅkṣitaṃ hṛdisthaṃ te tat sarvaṃ saṃbhaviṣyati
english: Nor should you give way to wrath: a blessing has drawn near to you. Whatever is wished for, set in your heart, all of it shall come to be."

sanskrit: ity evam uktaḥ kuśikaḥ prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā provāca muniśārdūlam idaṃ vacanam arthavat
english: Thus addressed, Kuśika, with inmost soul rejoicing, spoke to that tiger among sages this word fraught with meaning:

sanskrit: na me manyur mahābhāga pūto 'smi bhagavaṃs tvayā saṃvṛttau yauvanasthau svo vapuṣmantau balānvitau
english: "I bear no wrath, O greatly fortunate one; by you, venerable lord, I am made pure. We two have become young again, full of beauty and of strength.

sanskrit: pratodena vraṇā ye me sabhāryasya kṛtās tvayā tān na paśyāmi gātreṣu svastho 'smi saha bhāryayā
english: The wounds you made upon me and my wife with the goad—I see them no longer upon our limbs; I am whole again, together with my wife.

sanskrit: imāṃ ca devīṃ paśyāmi mune divyāpsaropamām śriyā paramayā yuktāṃ yathādṛṣṭāṃ mayā purā
english: And this lady I behold, O sage, like a celestial apsaras, endowed with surpassing beauty, even as I saw her of old.

sanskrit: tava prasādāt saṃvṛttam idaṃ sarvaṃ mahāmune naitac citraṃ tu bhagavaṃs tvayi satyaparākrama
english: By your grace has all this come to pass, O great sage; yet this is no wonder in you, O venerable one whose valor is truth."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ pratyuvācedaṃ cyavanaḥ kuśikaṃ tadā āgacchethāḥ sabhāryaś ca tvam iheti narādhipa
english: Thus addressed, Cyavana then replied to Kuśika: "You shall come here, and with your wife," O lord of men.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ samanujñāto rājarṣir abhivādya tam prayayau vapuṣā yukto nagaraṃ devarājavat
english: Thus addressed and given leave, the royal sage saluted him and set forth, endowed with beauty, toward the city, like the king of the gods.

sanskrit: tata enam upājagmur amātyāḥ sapurohitāḥ balasthā gaṇikāyuktāḥ sarvāḥ prakṛtayas tathā
english: Then there came forth to meet him the ministers with the household priests, the men of the army, the courtesans, and all the orders of the realm as well.

sanskrit: tair vṛtaḥ kuśiko rājā śriyā paramayā jvalan praviveśa puraṃ hṛṣṭaḥ pūjyamāno 'tha bandibhiḥ
english: Encircled by them, King Kuśika, blazing with surpassing splendor, entered the city, gladdened, honored by the bards.

sanskrit: tataḥ praviśya nagaraṃ kṛtvā sarvāhṇikakriyāḥ bhuktvā sabhāryo rajanīm uvāsa sa mahīpatiḥ
english: Then, having entered the city and performed all the rites of the day, that lord of earth, with his wife, dined and passed the night.

sanskrit: tatas tu tau navam abhivīkṣya yauvanaṃ; parasparaṃ vigatajarāv ivāmarau nanandatuḥ śayanagatau vapurdharau; śriyā yutau dvijavaradattayā tayā
english: Then the two, beholding their renewed youth in each other, rejoiced like immortals freed of age, beautiful of form upon their couch, endowed with that splendor bestowed by the best of brahmans.

sanskrit: sa cāpy ṛṣir bhṛgukulakīrtivardhanas; tapodhano vanam abhirāmam ṛddhimat manīṣayā bahuvidharatnabhūṣitaṃ; sasarja yan nāsti śatakrator api
english: And that sage too, the increaser of the Bhṛgu line's renown, rich in penance, fashioned by the power of his mind a delightful, flourishing forest, adorned with jewels of many kinds, such as is not found even with the lord of a hundred sacrifices.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tataḥ sa rājā rātryante pratibuddho mahāmanāḥ kṛtapūrvāhṇikaḥ prāyāt sabhāryas tad vanaṃ prati
english: Bhīṣma said: Then that high-minded king, awakened at the close of night, having performed the morning rites, set out with his wife toward that forest.

sanskrit: tato dadarśa nṛpatiḥ prāsādaṃ sarvakāñcanam maṇistambhasahasrāḍhyaṃ gandharvanagaropamam tatra divyān abhiprāyān dadarśa kuśikas tadā
english: Then the king beheld a palace all of gold, rich with a thousand jeweled pillars, like a city of the gandharvas; and there Kuśika beheld marvels of celestial design.

sanskrit: parvatān ramyasānūṃś ca nalinīś ca sapaṅkajāḥ citraśālāś ca vividhās toraṇāni ca bhārata śādvalopacitāṃ bhūmiṃ tathā kāñcanakuṭṭimām
english: Mountains with lovely peaks, and lotus-pools bearing their blossoms, and picture-galleries of many kinds, and gateways, O Bhārata, and ground heaped with fresh turf, paved too with gold.

sanskrit: sahakārān praphullāṃś ca ketakoddālakān dhavān aśokān mucukundāṃś ca phullāṃś caivātimuktakān
english: Mango trees in full bloom, ketakas, uddālakas, dhavas, aśokas, and mucukundas, and atimuktakas all flowering,

sanskrit: campakāṃs tilakān bhavyān panasān vañjulān api puṣpitān karṇikārāṃś ca tatra tatra dadarśa ha
english: campakas, splendid tilakas, jackfruit trees, and vañjulas too, and karṇikāras in flower—these he beheld here and there.

sanskrit: śyāmāṃ vāraṇapuṣpīṃ ca tathāṣṭāpadikāṃ latām tatra tatra parikḷptā dadarśa sa mahīpatiḥ
english: The śyāmā creeper, the vāraṇapuṣpī, and the aṣṭāpadikā vine, set out here and there—these that lord of earth beheld.

sanskrit: vṛkṣān padmotpaladharān sarvartukusumāṃs tathā vimānacchandakāṃś cāpi prāsādān padmasaṃnibhān
english: Trees bearing lotuses and water-lilies, and others blossoming in every season, and palaces shaped like celestial cars, mansions resembling lotuses,

sanskrit: śītalāni ca toyāni kva cid uṣṇāni bhārata āsanāni vicitrāṇi śayanapravarāṇi ca
english: and waters cool, and in some places warm, O Bhārata, and seats of varied work, and couches of the choicest kind,

sanskrit: paryaṅkān sarvasauvarṇān parārdhyāstaraṇāstṛtān bhakṣyabhojyam anantaṃ ca tatra tatropakalpitam
english: divans all of gold, spread over with coverlets of priceless worth, and food to be eaten and to be enjoyed without end, made ready here and there.

sanskrit: vāṇīvādāñ chukāṃś cāpi śārikābhṛṅgarājakān kokilāñ chatapatrāṃś ca koyaṣṭimakakukkuṭān
english: Sweet-voiced parrots too, and śārikā mynas and bhṛṅgarāja birds, cuckoos and woodpeckers, sandpipers and jungle-fowl,

sanskrit: mayūrān kukkuṭāṃś cāpi putrakāñ jīvajīvakān cakorān vānarān haṃsān sārasāṃś cakrasāhvayān
english: peacocks and wild-cocks, putraka birds and jīvaṃjīvakas, cakora partridges, monkeys, swans, sārasa cranes, and the birds named after the cakravāka,

sanskrit: samantataḥ praṇaditān dadarśa sumanoharān kva cid apsarasāṃ saṃghān gandharvāṇāṃ ca pārthiva
english: crying out on every side, most charming—these he beheld, and in some places throngs of apsarases and of gandharvas, O king.

sanskrit: kāntābhir aparāṃs tatra pariṣvaktān dadarśa ha na dadarśa ca tān bhūyo dadarśa ca punar nṛpaḥ
english: Others he beheld there embraced by their beloved ones; and then he saw them no more, and again the king saw them once more.

sanskrit: gītadhvaniṃ sumadhuraṃ tathaivādhyayanadhvanim haṃsān sumadhurāṃś cāpi tatra śuśrāva pārthivaḥ
english: The sweet sound of song, and likewise the sound of recitation, and the swans most sweet of voice—these the king heard there.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvātyadbhutaṃ rājā manasācintayat tadā svapno 'yaṃ cittavibhraṃśa utāho satyam eva tu
english: Beholding that exceeding marvel, the king then pondered within his mind: "Is this a dream, a derangement of the mind, or is it truly real?

sanskrit: aho saha śarīreṇa prāpto 'smi paramāṃ gatim uttarān vā kurūn puṇyān atha vāpy amarāvatīm
english: Ah, in this very body have I reached the supreme abode—the holy Northern Kurus, or else Amarāvatī itself!

sanskrit: kiṃ tv idaṃ mahad āścaryaṃ saṃpaśyāmīty acintayat evaṃ saṃcintayann eva dadarśa munipuṃgavam
english: Yet what is this great wonder that I behold?"—so he mused. And even as he mused thus, he beheld the bull among sages,

sanskrit: tasmin vimāne sauvarṇe maṇistambhasamākule mahārhe śayane divye śayānaṃ bhṛgunandanam
english: the delight of the Bhṛgus, reclining in that golden car thronged with jeweled pillars, upon a precious, celestial couch.

sanskrit: tam abhyayāt praharṣeṇa narendraḥ saha bhāryayā antarhitas tato bhūyaś cyavanaḥ śayanaṃ ca tat
english: Toward him the lord of men, with his wife, drew near in great joy; whereupon Cyavana vanished once again, and that couch as well.

sanskrit: tato 'nyasmin vanoddeśe punar eva dadarśa tam kauśyāṃ bṛsyāṃ samāsīnaṃ japamānaṃ mahāvratam evaṃ yogabalād vipro mohayām āsa pārthivam
english: Then in another quarter of the forest he beheld him once more, seated upon a couch of kuśa grass, murmuring his prayers, steadfast in his great vow. Thus, by the power of yoga, the brahman bewildered the king.
